message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) along the I‑5 corridor. Under normal conditions—steady traffic, no major detours, and staying within speed limits—the trip usually takes around **6 hours**.  

If you’re heading out during rush hour or on a weekend when traffic can be heavier, you might add an extra hour or two. Conversely, if you’re traveling on a clear day with minimal stops, you could get there in about **5½ hours**.  

A quick way to get a more precise estimate is to plug your departure time into a navigation app (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps) which will factor in real‑time traffic and give you a dynamic ETA.

We can provide approximate driving distance (~383 miles via I-5) and typical driving time (~6 hours). But we might also mention traffic, speed limits, etc. No function call needed. Just answer.
